Bank Of Maharashtra has informed the Exchange that the  Bank's Board had approved  equity investment not exceeding  of Rs. 6.00 crore  in the Global Trade Finance Pvt Ltd in the meeting held on 31.1.2004 subject to the approval of the Reserve Bank of India.   Global Trade Finance Private Limited is established by WestLB AG, Exim Bank and IFC Washington to undertake factoring and forfaiting for the Indian exporters.The Company has commenced operations in September 2001. Its authorised capital is Rs.45 crore and the same was held by WestLB 40%, Exim Bank 35% and IFC 25%.  Now WestLB has decided to divest its stake and IFC has decided to reduce its stake to 12.50%, Exim Bank has decided to increase its stake to 40% and FIMBank has decided to take stake of 38.5%. As regards  the balance 9% equity stake, the Bank had decided to acquire the same and had  approached the RBI for approval.The RBI, Foreign Exchange Department, Mumbai vide letter dated July 06,2004 has conveyed approval under FEMA 1999 for the above investment. Accordingly, the Bank has entered into an agreement to purchase 40,50,000 shares of face value Rs. 10/- each at a price of Rs. 12.50 per share aggregating to Rs.5,06,25,000/- or rupee equivalent to US Dollars 10,63,125.00 whichever is less from West LB. With this investment, the bank's equity stake will be 9% in the Global Trade Finance Pvt Ltd..
